senses.definition: (uncountable) A black or brownish black rock formed from prehistoric plant remains, composed largely of carbon and burned as a fuel.
examples: The coal in this region was prized by ironmasters in centuries past, who mined it in the spots where the drainage methods of the day permitted.

quotes.text: Coal-eaters they may have been, but a more willing or harder working Atlantic engine was never designed.

subsenses.definition: (countable) A type of coal, such as bituminous, anthracite, or lignite, and grades and varieties thereof, as a fuel commodity ready to buy and burn.
examples: Put some coal on the fire.
Order some coal from the coalyard.

senses.definition: (countable) A piece of coal used for burning (this use is less common in American English)
examples: Put some coals on the fire.

senses.definition: (countable) A glowing or charred piece of coal, wood, or other solid fuel.
examples: Just as the campfire died down to just coals, with no flames to burn the marshmallows, someone dumped a whole load of wood on, so I gave up and went to bed.
I'm so sick of seeing this coal online.
